The react-v0 branch shipped 0.70.0 (2025-10-30, breaking: Fela renderer reworked to useInsertionEffect), 0.71.0 (2025-11-03, breaking: Popup animations removed + React 19/Concurrent fixes), 0.71.1 (2025-11-20), 0.71.2 (2026-02-25) and 0.71.3 (2026-02-25, a FEATURE: @container query support in Fela renderer). compat.ie11: v8 is the LAST Fluent React line with any IE11 story. Microsoft: 'Starting on June 15th, 2022, Fluent UI v8 will no longer support Internet Explorer 11 or earlier... any changes made to the library from June 15th, 2022 onward may break compatibility with Internet Explorer 11.' and 'There are no plans to remove existing IE11 compatibility from Fluent UI v8. Any breaks to Fluent UI v8's IE11 compatibility will likely be the result of bug fixes.' v9 NEVER supported IE11 (RFC rfcs/react-components/convergence/ending-ie11-support.md). Practical advice: an IE11-bound team must pin @fluentui/react to a pre-2022-06-15 8.x and accept no updates.

apis.name: createTheme
apis.use: Pure, side-effect-free theme builder. Fills every slot from DefaultPalette/DefaultEffects/DefaultFontStyles/DefaultSpacing, then mergeThemes(base, partial). Emit this from generators and pass the result to ThemeProvider.
apis.pitfall: mergeThemes recomputes semanticColors from partialTheme.palette ONLY, so a partial palette yields a mixed theme where unmapped semantics keep default-blue values. Always supply all 50 palette slots. Also: if palette.themePrimary is set without palette.accent, accent is auto-set to themePrimary. depComments=true appends the literal string ' /* @deprecated */' to deprecated color VALUES - never enable programmatically.

apis.name: loadTheme
apis.use: Global, app-wide theme application. Sets the module singleton, runs legacy @microsoft/load-themed-styles token replacement over registered SCSS, applies Customizations settings, and fires all onThemeChange callbacks. Required only if the app has styles relying on @microsoft/load-themed-styles.
apis.pitfall: Module-level singleton - last call wins app-wide, cannot be scoped or nested. Must run before first render to avoid FOUC. The legacy SCSS token pass is a perf cost and is hard to undo. Officially superseded by ThemeProvider.

apis.name: getTheme
apis.use: Reads the loadTheme singleton. Use for non-React code that needs the current theme.
apis.pitfall: Passing depComments=true REPLACES the singleton with a fresh default theme, silently discarding whatever was loaded. Also does not see themes provided only via <ThemeProvider> - use useTheme() inside components.

apis.name: ThemeProvider
apis.signature: <ThemeProvider theme?: PartialTheme | Theme, applyTo?: 'element' | 'body' | 'none', as?: React.ElementType, ref?: React.Ref<HTMLElement>>
apis.use: The recommended, non-deprecated way to theme v8. Merges with the parent theme via mergeThemes(parentTheme, userTheme), provides ThemeContext + CustomizerContext + FocusRectsProvider, and is the ONLY mechanism that applies theme.components (component-level styles). Nestable for sectional theming.
apis.pitfall: Does NOT emit CSS custom properties - it applies a merge-styles class with literal values for bodyText/bodyBackground/fonts.medium (CSS variables are a v9/Griffel feature). Renders a real <div> by default (use as={React.Fragment} to avoid layout impact). The merge is memoized on theme object identity, so an inline object literal re-merges every render. Does not fire registerOnThemeChangeCallback.

apis.name: Customizer
apis.signature: <Customizer settings={{ theme }} scopedSettings={{ ComponentName: { styles } }} contextTransform?>
apis.use: Legacy pre-v8 theming. Only for maintaining existing code; migrate settings={{theme}} -> ThemeProvider theme={}, and scopedSettings={{X:{styles}}} -> theme={{components:{X:{styles}}}}.
apis.pitfall: Explicitly @deprecated as of @fluentui/react v8 for theming purposes; will be removed in v9. Merges customizations rather than deep-merging themes, so a partial theme replaces rather than layers onto the ambient theme. Only reaches components wrapped by customizable()/styled(), and forceUpdates on every global Customizations change.

apis.name: useTheme
apis.use: React hook to read the active theme inside function components. Resolution order: ThemeContext -> Customizer/Customizations (incl. loadTheme) -> createTheme({}). Never returns undefined. Class components use <ThemeContext.Consumer>.
apis.pitfall: The final fallback allocates a brand-new default theme on every call when no provider exists, so an unwrapped component silently renders with default Fluent blue instead of erroring.

apis.name: registerOnThemeChangeCallback
apis.use: Subscribe to global theme changes for code that cannot react through React state. Paired with removeOnThemeChangeCallback(callback). De-duplicates by function identity.
apis.pitfall: Fires ONLY from loadTheme - a <ThemeProvider theme={}> change never triggers it. Callbacks are wrapped in try/catch so a throwing callback fails silently. Must be manually removed or it leaks.

themeGeneration.algorithm: Three base slots drive everything: primaryColor (brand), backgroundColor, foregroundColor (text). themeRulesStandardCreator() builds an IThemeRules graph where each of 23 FabricSlots inherits from one base slot at a given Shade (1-8, or Unshaded), plus an isBackgroundShade flag for background-derived slots. Defaults: primaryColor #0078d4, backgroundColor #ffffff, foregroundColor #323130. Slot->(base,Shade,isBackgroundShade) from the ACTUAL _makeFabricSlotRule calls (the enum comments disagree and are wrong): themePrimary(primary,Unshaded), themeLighterAlt(primary,1), themeLighter(primary,2), themeLight(primary,3), themeTertiary(primary,4), themeSecondary(primary,5), themeDarkAlt(primary,6), themeDark(primary,7), themeDarker(primary,8), neutralLighterAlt(bg,1,BG), neutralLighter(bg,2,BG), neutralLight(bg,3,BG), neutralQuaternaryAlt(bg,4,BG), neutralQuaternary(bg,5,BG), neutralTertiaryAlt(bg,6,BG), neutralTertiary(fg,3), neutralSecondary(fg,4), neutralSecondaryAlt(fg,4), neutralPrimaryAlt(fg,5), neutralPrimary(fg,Unshaded), neutralDark(fg,7), black(fg,8), white(bg,Unshaded,BG). getShade(color,shade,isInverted): convert to HSV via rgb2hsv (h integer degrees, s/v integer percent - this rounding is lossy and must be replicated); compute hsl=hsv2hsl(h,s,v); tableIndex=shade-1; soften=lighten, strongen=darken (swapped when isInverted). Branch: pure white -> darken(WhiteShadeTable[i]); pure black -> lighten(BlackTintTable[i]); hsl.l/100>0.8 -> strongen(LumShadeTable[i]); hsl.l/100<0.2 -> soften(LumTintTable[i]); else default -> i<5 ? soften(ColorTintTable[i]) : strongen(ColorShadeTable[i-5]). Tables: WhiteShadeTableBG=[0.027,0.043,0.082,0.145,0.184,0.216,0.349,0.537]; BlackTintTableBG=[0.537,0.45,0.349,0.216,0.184,0.145,0.082,0.043]; WhiteShadeTable=[0.537,0.349,0.216,0.184,0.145,0.082,0.043,0.027]; BlackTintTable=[0.537,0.45,0.349,0.216,0.184,0.145,0.082,0.043]; LumTintTable=[0.88,0.77,0.66,0.55,0.44,0.33,0.22,0.11]; LumShadeTable=[0.11,0.22,0.33,0.44,0.55,0.66,0.77,0.88]; ColorTintTable=[0.96,0.84,0.7,0.4,0.12]; ColorShadeTable=[0.1,0.24,0.44]. darken(hsv,f)={h,s,v:clamp(v-v*f,100,0)} (does NOT change s); lighten(hsv,f)={h,s:clamp(s-s*f,100,0),v:clamp(v+(100-v)*f,100,0)}. Then hsv2rgb with Math.round(255*(x+m)). getBackgroundShade(color,shade,isInverted): !isInverted -> darken(WhiteShadeTableBG[shade-1]); isInverted -> lighten(BlackTintTableBG[8-shade]). isDark(color) = hsv2hsl(h,s,v).l < 50. RECIPE from one brand hex: const rules=themeRulesStandardCreator(); ThemeGenerator.insureSlots(rules,false); ThemeGenerator.setSlot(rules['primaryColor'], getColorFromString(brandHex), false, /*isCustomization*/true, /*overwriteCustomColor*/true); const palette=ThemeGenerator.getThemeAsJson(rules); const theme=createTheme({palette, isInverted:isDark(bgColor)}). Leaving foreground/background untouched keeps the hand-tuned Fluent neutrals because themeRulesStandardCreator pre-seeds 22 slots with isCustomized=true, which insureSlots (overwriteCustomColor=false) preserves but a base-color change (overwriteCustomColor=true) overwrites. CRITICAL: the generated ramp differs from DefaultPalette - #0078d4 generates themeLighterAlt #f3f9fd and themeLighter #d0e7f8, not #eff6fc/#deecf9, because DefaultPalette is hand-tuned. Also getThemeAsJson returns MORE than 23 keys (it also emits primaryColor, primaryColorShade1..8, backgroundColor/Shade1..8, foregroundColor/Shade1..8) - filter to FabricSlots. getThemeAsJson uses rule.color.str (preserves the user's original input string, e.g. 'red'); use rule.color.hex for deterministic '#rrggbb' output. getColorFromString requires a DOM Document (pass one or pre-parse in Node/SSR) and hex must be '#'-prefixed. The designer never generates accent, blackTranslucent40, whiteTranslucent40, or any of the 24 status colors - those fall back to DefaultPalette via createTheme.

darkTheme.howProduced: createTheme({ palette: DarkDefaultPalette, semanticColors: {...13 overrides}, isInverted: true }) as shipped in @fluentui/theme-samples DarkCustomizations
darkTheme.note: isInverted:true alone does NOT invert the palette - createTheme({isInverted:true}) returns the identical light palette; only ~19 hard-coded invariant semantic slots and cardShadowHovered change. You must supply an explicit inverted palette (ramp is reversed: themeDarker is the lightest blue, black is #ffffff, white is #1b1a19). Microsoft's own sample additionally overrides 13 semanticColors (buttonText, menuBackground, menuItemBackgroundHovered/Pressed, menuDivider, menuIcon, menuHeader, menuItemText/Hovered, disabledBackground, inputBackgroundChecked, buttonTextPressed/Hovered) and 15 component styles, which is evidence that palette + isInverted alone is not sufficient for a usable dark theme. Only 24 of 50 palette slots are defined in the official dark sample; the status/accent colors (yellow, orange, magenta, purple, blue, teal, green families) and accent/translucent slots are left at their light-theme defaults - those are null in the palette map above. High contrast is separate and theme-independent: v8 handles it via HighContrastSelector ('@media screen and (-ms-high-contrast: active), screen and (forced-colors: active)'), HighContrastSelectorWhite/Black, and getHighContrastNoAdjustStyle(), using CSS system keywords (WindowText, Window, Highlight, HighlightText, GrayText, ButtonText, ButtonFace) rather than theme slots - so a v8 theme JSON has no HC fields.

visualTells: DevTools: CSS classes start with ms- (ms-Button, ms-Icon, ms-Layer, ms-Fabric) plus mergeStyles hashes like root-123. Fluent 2 emits fui- prefixes (fui-Button, fui-Button__icon).
No CSS custom properties anywhere: v8 mergeStyles emits static classes. Fluent 2's FluentProvider element carries hundreds of token vars. Zero --fui-* vars on any ancestor means Fluent 1.
Default button corner-radius computes to 2px in Fluent 1 and 4px in Fluent 2. Inspect any secondary button.
Icons render as <i class="ms-Icon" data-icon-name="Add"> using an icon font. Fluent 2 renders inline <svg>.
Primary/accent blue is #0078d4 in Fluent 1 and #0f6cbd in Fluent 2. Eyedrop any primary button.
Animation durations in computed styles read 0.167s / 0.267s / 0.367s / 0.467s. Nothing in Fluent 2 uses these; Fluent 2 uses round 100ms-500ms values.
box-shadow uses fractional pixels and odd opacities: 0 1.6px 3.6px rgba(0,0,0,.132). Fluent 2 uses whole px plus an offsetless 0 0 2px ambient layer.
Portalled content sits in <div class="ms-Layer ms-Layer--fixed"> appended to end of <body> with z-index 1000000.
Body text has no explicit line-height (inherits browser default). Fluent 2 always sets one, e.g. 20px for 14px text.
All text at 20px and above is weight 600; everything 18px and below is 400. Fluent 2 varies weight independently of size.

Focus ring is a square white-inner + #605e5c-outer double ring drawn on an ::after pseudo-element, and only appears once the body carries a ms-Fabric--isFocusVisible class. Fluent 2's ring is brand-colored and rounded to 4px.
Network tab shows @font-face WOFF/WOFF2 downloads from res-1.cdn.office.net/files/fabric-cdn-prod_*. Fluent 2 never fetches fonts.
Root app wrapper is <Fabric> or v8 ThemeProvider emitting ms-Fabric, not <FluentProvider>.
Only 4 elevation levels exist in the stylesheet (4/8/16/64); no shadow2 or shadow28 equivalents.
Signature components on screen: CommandBar, DetailsList, Pivot, Nav, Persona, Panel, and Callouts with a pointed beak. Fluent 2 shows Toolbar, DataGrid, TabList, Drawer, Avatar, Popover.
Spacing rhythm only ever lands on 4/8/16/20/32px; no 2, 6, 10, 12 or 24px steps appear.
Pills and circles are hand-rolled with inline borderRadius 50% because v8 has no circular radius token.
package.json depends on @fluentui/react ^8.x or office-ui-fabric-react, not @fluentui/react-components ^9.x.
Icons look thin and angular with a single outline weight; Fluent 2 icons are rounder and come in matched Regular/Filled pairs where filled marks selection.

keyboardPatterns.pattern: Outer FocusZone direction=vertical with shouldEnterInnerZone=isRightArrow. Up/Down moves rows; Right enters the row's inner zone to reach cells; Up from the first row jumps to the header; Down from the header returns to the list and auto-selects index 0 when isSelectedOnFocus and nothing is selected.
keyboardPatterns.roles: role defaults to 'grid'; List/GroupedList get role=presentation; rows are isGridRow with id row-{index}

keyboardPatterns.pattern: FocusZone direction=horizontal with role=menubar. Left/Right move between commands, Enter/Space activate, Down opens a submenu ContextualMenu. Items get role=menuitem and allowDisabledFocus=true so disabled commands stay discoverable.
keyboardPatterns.roles: root menubar; OverflowSet role=group when far items exist else none; overflow button role=menuitem

keyboardPatterns.pattern: Rendered in Callout inside a Layer with shouldFocusOnMount defaulting to true. Up/Down move items, Right opens a submenu, Left or Escape closes. subMenuHoverDelay governs pointer opening.
keyboardPatterns.roles: menu/menuitem; item types Normal, Divider, Header, Section
requiredLabels: id (documented as the value to use for aria-owns)

keyboardPatterns.pattern: FocusZone direction=vertical wrapping <nav role=navigation aria-label>. Up/Down move links, Enter activates, group headers toggle collapse. Links render as ActionButton so button semantics are preserved.
keyboardPatterns.roles: role defaults to 'navigation'; selected link gets aria-current defaulting to 'page'

keyboardPatterns.pattern: FocusZone across the tab headers. Left/Right move between tabs, Enter/Space select. Tab ids come from getTabId as {pivotId}-Tab{index} and are wired to panels via aria-labelledby.
keyboardPatterns.roles: each header role=tab with aria-selected; a custom link.role other than 'tab' SUPPRESSES aria-selected
requiredLabels: aria-label or aria-labelledby on the Pivot

keyboardPatterns.pattern: Roving tabindex: the group is one Tab stop, arrows move within. shouldRaiseClicks (default true) walks up the DOM firing click on Enter/Space for elements that are not real buttons.
requiredLabels: aria-label or aria-labelledby on the zone container when it carries a composite role

commonGaps.issue: Icon-only button with no accessible name
commonGaps.detect: Grep for IconButton, CommandBarButton with iconOnly, or ActionButton carrying iconProps but no ariaLabel/aria-label/title. In the DOM the rendered <i class="ms-Icon"> has aria-hidden="true" and the button's accessible name is empty.
commonGaps.fix: Add ariaLabel to the button (not the Icon). v8's Icon auto-sets aria-hidden when unnamed, so the button must carry the name.

commonGaps.issue: initializeIcons() never called
commonGaps.detect: No import of initializeIcons from @fluentui/font-icons-mdl2 or @fluentui/react/lib/Icons anywhere in the entry file; every icon renders as a placeholder box and data-icon-name is present but no glyph paints.
commonGaps.fix: Call initializeIcons() once at app startup.

commonGaps.issue: Callout rendered with no role
commonGaps.detect: Grep <Callout without a role prop. In the DOM the callout content is a bare div inside .ms-Layer with no dialog/menu semantics.
commonGaps.fix: Set role="dialog" (or alertdialog) plus ariaLabelledBy or ariaLabel.

commonGaps.issue: FocusZone with no explicit direction
commonGaps.detect: Grep <FocusZone that has no direction prop. It silently defaults to FocusZoneDirection.bidirectional and performs geometric focus math.
commonGaps.fix: Set direction explicitly: vertical for lists/menus, horizontal for toolbars/tabs, domOrder for wrapping lists.

commonGaps.issue: Menu-like FocusZone without isCircularNavigation
commonGaps.detect: A FocusZone wrapping role=menu or role=menubar children with no isCircularNavigation prop; arrowing past the last item dead-ends.
commonGaps.fix: Add isCircularNavigation. ARIA APG requires wrapping in menus.

commonGaps.issue: Standalone FocusTrapZone without enableAriaHiddenSiblings
commonGaps.detect: Grep <FocusTrapZone not inside Modal/Panel/Dialog and lacking enableAriaHiddenSiblings. Focus is trapped but sibling DOM has no aria-hidden, so a virtual cursor still reads the page behind.
commonGaps.fix: Add enableAriaHiddenSiblings, or use Modal/Dialog/Panel which handle it.

commonGaps.issue: enableAriaHiddenSiblings explicitly set to false
commonGaps.detect: Grep enableAriaHiddenSiblings={false} on Modal, Panel or Popup.
commonGaps.fix: Remove the override. The source marks false as deprecated: it breaks modal behaviour for some screen readers and will not be supported.

commonGaps.issue: FocusZone handleTabKey creating a keyboard trap
commonGaps.detect: Grep handleTabKey={FocusZoneTabbableElements.all} or the deprecated allowTabKey. The v8 source itself calls the inability to Tab out an 'unfortunate side effect'.
commonGaps.fix: Remove handleTabKey, or guarantee an Escape key exit path out of the zone.

commonGaps.issue: Focus indicator destroyed by missing Fabric/ThemeProvider
commonGaps.detect: App renders v8 controls without a <Fabric> / v8 ThemeProvider ancestor, so no ms-Fabric--isFocusVisible class is ever applied. v8 already sets outline: transparent, so tabbing shows nothing at all.
commonGaps.fix: Wrap the app in ThemeProvider/Fabric so FocusRects applies the isFocusVisible class.

commonGaps.issue: Custom styles override drops getFocusStyle
commonGaps.detect: A styles prop replaces a component's root array without spreading getFocusStyle(theme, ...), or app CSS sets outline: none / outline: 0 on ms-* selectors. Tab and observe no ::after ring.
commonGaps.fix: Re-include getFocusStyle(theme, { inset, highContrastStyle, borderColor }) in the root style, and never re-clear outline.

commonGaps.issue: Focus ring below 3:1 contrast
commonGaps.detect: Default ring is 1px border palette.white plus 1px outline palette.neutralSecondary (#605e5c). On mid-tone or brand-colored backgrounds sample the ring against its surround.
commonGaps.fix: Pass borderColor/outlineColor/width via getFocusStyle options to reach 3:1.

commonGaps.issue: No prefers-reduced-motion handling
commonGaps.detect: Grep for prefers-reduced-motion in app and theme CSS. v8's AnimationStyles contains none, so all ~40 slide/fade/scale animations run unconditionally.
commonGaps.fix: Wrap AnimationStyles usage in a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override setting animation/transition duration to ~0.01ms.

commonGaps.issue: Legacy -ms-high-contrast CSS with no forced-colors clause
commonGaps.detect: Grep app CSS for '-ms-high-contrast' and check the same at-rule does not also list 'forced-colors: active'. Such blocks are dead in modern Chromium/Edge.
commonGaps.fix: Use HighContrastSelector from @fluentui/style-utilities, or add the forced-colors clause.

commonGaps.issue: role="application" on DetailsList
commonGaps.detect: Grep shouldApplyApplicationRole on DetailsList, or role="application" in the rendered root. It forces screen readers into forms/application mode and kills browse navigation.
commonGaps.fix: Remove shouldApplyApplicationRole; it is deprecated.

commonGaps.issue: shouldFocusOnContainer on ContextualMenu
commonGaps.detect: Grep shouldFocusOnContainer. The v8 source comment warns it 'breaks the default focus behaviour when using assistive technologies'.
commonGaps.fix: Remove it and let focus land on the first menu item.

commonGaps.issue: Layer content with no aria relationship to its trigger
commonGaps.detect: A Callout/Panel/ContextualMenu portals into .ms-Layer at end of body while the trigger button has no aria-expanded, aria-controls or aria-owns pointing at the menu id.
commonGaps.fix: Set aria-expanded and aria-controls (or aria-owns) on the trigger using the ContextualMenu id prop, and/or use LayerHost + hostId to keep DOM order sane.

commonGaps.issue: Ancestor keyboard handler never fires for layered content
commonGaps.detect: A global onKeyDown/Escape handler on a wrapper stops working once content moves inside Callout/Panel/Modal. Layer stops ~30 React events including onKeyDown, onFocus and onBlur by default.
commonGaps.fix: Set eventBubblingEnabled on the Layer, or use Popup's onDismiss which owns Escape.

commonGaps.issue: Overlay used alone as a modal
commonGaps.detect: Grep <Overlay not accompanied by FocusTrapZone/Modal. The scrim renders with no role, no focus trap and no Escape handling.
commonGaps.fix: Use Modal, or pair Overlay with FocusTrapZone plus role=dialog and aria-modal.

commonGaps.issue: Async content changes with no live region
commonGaps.detect: Search/filter/sort/save flows that mutate results with no <Announced> mounted and no role=alert region. Screen readers announce nothing.
commonGaps.fix: Keep one <Announced> mounted and update its message; vary the string so repeats are announced.

commonGaps.issue: Announced re-rendered with an identical message
commonGaps.detect: message prop is a constant string or the same computed value across updates; nothing is announced on repeat events.
commonGaps.fix: Include a changing token (count, timestamp) so the live region text actually mutates.

commonGaps.issue: Announced set to aria-live="assertive"
commonGaps.detect: Grep aria-live="assertive" on Announced. The root hard-codes role="status", producing a contradictory role/live pairing.
commonGaps.fix: Use a custom role="alert" region for genuinely urgent messages.

commonGaps.issue: Pivot item with a custom role other than tab
commonGaps.detect: Grep role on PivotItem headers. The v8 source drops aria-selected in that branch, so the selected tab is never announced as selected.
commonGaps.fix: Keep role="tab", or supply aria-selected yourself.

commonGaps.issue: Nav linkAs/onRenderLink replacing ActionButton with a div
commonGaps.detect: Grep linkAs or onRenderLink on Nav returning a div or span. Button semantics and aria-current are lost.
commonGaps.fix: Render a real button or anchor and preserve aria-current on the selected link.

commonGaps.issue: DetailsList missing grid and checkbox labels
commonGaps.detect: Grep <DetailsList lacking ariaLabelForGrid, ariaLabelForSelectAllCheckbox, ariaLabelForSelectionColumn and checkButtonAriaLabel. The grid and its selection column announce as unlabeled.
commonGaps.fix: Supply all four props plus getRowAriaLabel for row context.

commonGaps.issue: DetailsList column reorder or Modal drag with no keyboard path
commonGaps.detect: columnReorderOptions is set on DetailsList, or Modal dragOptions is supplied without keyboardMoveIconProps/moveMenuItemText/menu wired up. Try reordering with the keyboard only.
commonGaps.fix: Wire the IDragOptions keyboard menu, or provide an explicit non-drag alternative.

commonGaps.issue: Deprecated ariaLabel prop on Icon
commonGaps.detect: Grep <Icon ariaLabel= (capital L). IIconProps.ariaLabel is deprecated in favour of the native attribute.
commonGaps.fix: Use aria-label, or leave decorative icons unnamed so v8 sets aria-hidden.

commonGaps.issue: Meaningful icon named twice / decorative icon named
commonGaps.detect: An Icon carries aria-label while its parent button also has ariaLabel, producing role=img duplicate announcements; or a purely decorative Icon is labeled.
commonGaps.fix: Name the interactive ancestor only; leave decorative Icons unnamed.

commonGaps.issue: Custom theme changes themePrimary without contrast re-check
commonGaps.detect: createTheme or loadTheme overrides palette.themePrimary. v8 performs no contrast validation on custom palettes.
commonGaps.fix: Re-measure text and non-text contrast after any palette override; the stock #0078d4 already sits close to the 4.5:1 threshold.

commonGaps.issue: FocusZone becomes unreachable when the active item is hidden
commonGaps.detect: A list where the last-focused item can be filtered or hidden; afterwards Tab skips the whole zone because the roving tabindex remains on a hidden element.
commonGaps.fix: Reset the zone via componentRef.focus(true) or defaultTabbableElement when items change.

fluent2ThemeForV8.description: Official Microsoft package: 'A Fluent2 theme for Fluent UI React 8.x'. Lets a v8 app adopt the Fluent 2 LOOK without migrating to v9.
fluent2ThemeForV8.whatItDoes: Exports Fluent2WebLightTheme and Fluent2WebDarkTheme, built via createTheme({ palette, semanticColors, components: fluent2ComponentStyles, effects }). It replaces the v8 palette with Fluent 2 colors (themePrimary #0f6cbd, neutral ramp #141414-#fafafa), overrides semantic color slots, swaps in Fluent 2 elevation shadows and rounded-corner radii (2/4/6/8px), and injects per-component style overrides for ~30 v8 components. Component styles ship inside the theme, so passing the theme to ThemeProvider is sufficient.
fluent2ThemeForV8.howToUse: import { ThemeProvider } from '@fluentui/react'; import { Fluent2WebLightTheme, Fluent2WebDarkTheme } from '@fluentui/fluent2-theme'; <ThemeProvider theme={Fluent2WebLightTheme}><App /></ThemeProvider>
fluent2ThemeForV8.componentsNotRestyled: Only the ~32 keys above have Fluent 2 style overrides. Everything else keeps the Fluent 1 look, notably: DetailsList/GroupedList (only DetailRowCheck and Check are covered), Panel, Nav, DatePicker, Calendar, ComboBox, Persona, Facepile, Rating, Link, Label, Tooltip, TeachingBubble, Coachmark, ProgressIndicator, ActivityItem, DocumentCard, Shimmer.
fluent2ThemeForV8.limitations: Cosmetic only. Does NOT: change any component API, props, DOM structure or behavior; swap MDL2 font icons for Fluent 2 icons (@fluentui/font-icons-mdl2 stays); add any v9 component; give you Griffel/design tokens; or make you compatible with v9 theming. Coverage is partial so mixed Fluent 1/Fluent 2 visuals are expected in apps using uncovered components. It is not a migration path and does not reduce eventual v8->v9 migration cost.
fluent2ThemeForV8.whenToRecommend: Users who are hard-pinned to v8 (SPFx, PCF Fluent 8, IE11-era constraints) and want to look current. Not a substitute for migrating to v9.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: Your app is a DetailsList app.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: `DataGrid` is stable but is not feature-equivalent: no built-in virtualization (v8 had it; you must add `@fluentui-contrib/react-data-grid-react-window`), no column drag-reorder (`IColumnReorderOptions`), no `ConstrainMode`, no `IDragDropEvents`, no `GroupedList` integration, no `ShimmeredDetailsList`. doNotMigrateYet.headline: Your app depends on HoverCard, Coachmark, MarqueeSelection, ResizeGroup, ScrollablePane+Sticky, ActivityItem, or ButtonGrid.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: Verified: no v9 equivalent, no compat package, no contrib package. You will be writing these from scratch.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: You use NormalPeoplePicker / ExtendedPeoplePicker / SelectedItemsList heavily.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: `TagPicker` is stable but is a different architecture — you own the async suggestion pipeline, and there are no people-specific affordances. Microsoft's table simultaneously says `PeoplePicker`→`TagPicker` and `Pickers`→"Not available", and lists `Pickers` as deprecated.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: You rely on Calendar/DatePicker/TimePicker.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: These exist only as `0.x` compat packages outside the `react-components` suite, where *minor version bumps are explicitly allowed to be breaking*. Not suitable for a codebase that can't tolerate churn.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: You use @fluentui/react-charting and want a pure-v9 stack.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: Charts are still v8 internally; you'll ship both libraries indefinitely and maintain a theme bridge.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: Your styling is heavily dynamic/runtime-computed
doNotMigrateYet.detail: (per-instance colors, computed selectors, `styled()` HOC theming, `IStyleFunctionOrObject` with state parameters). Griffel cannot compile these; you must enumerate variants, fall back to inline styles, or use CSS custom properties.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: You need v8 form validation semantics.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: v9 `Input`/`Textarea` deliberately have zero validation API (`errorMessage`, `onGetErrorMessage`, `validateOnFocusIn/Out/Load`, `deferredValidationTime`, `onNotifyValidationResult` all removed). You must adopt `Field` and/or an external form library.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: You cannot afford a mixed-bundle period and your app is large.
doNotMigrateYet.detail: The shim surface covers only Buttons/Checkbox/Stack/Theme, so incremental migration of everything else means genuine rewrites, and shims themselves pull in both libraries. Microsoft's own guidance is to avoid shims.

doNotMigrateYet.headline: A pragmatic partial-migration recipe
doNotMigrateYet.detail: that IS well supported today: keep v8 as the shell, add `FluentProvider` + `PortalCompatProvider` + `PortalMountNodeProvider`, bridge themes with `createV8Theme`, turn on `prefer-fluentui-v9` as a warning, and migrate leaf components (Button, Checkbox, Label, Text, Divider, Image, Spinner, Tooltip, Link, Persona, Badge, Switch, Rating) first — these are all `trivial`.
